{{Quote|I assume some of you are familiar with the recent problems on Tilnes and Ipsus. There is a virus, which has been manufactured in Cularin. It's about to be released into the atmosphere of a planet, where it will kill thousands of innocents. It won't discriminate. Young, old, sick, healthy&mdash;they'll all die. We've analyzed the virus. It will be deadly. And painful.|Osten Dal'Nay, on the anti-Caarite virus|<ref name="BOB" />}}
The '''anti-Caarite virus''', also known as the '''Tilnes virus''', was a deadly [[Bioengineering/Legends|bio-engineered]] plague that was designed to be [[Death/Legends|fatal]] to members of the [[Caarite]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The virus was developed by the [[Believers]] [[Sith cult]] around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], from a [[S-Ipsus Believers laboratory|laboratory]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Genarius]] in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]]. The [[Sith cultist/Legends|cultists]] sought to use the plague to commit [[Speciecide|genocide]] against the Caarites and thereby weaken the influence of the [[Metatheran Cartel]], a Caarite-dominated trade concern.

A test release of the virus was staged by the Believers at a [[Metatheran Cartel Tilnes base|Cartel base]] on [[Tilnes]], the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of the planet [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]]. The trial was largely successful and the plague wiped out hundreds of Caarites present in the installation, but had the unplanned side effect of causing [[Ko Bas]], the base's [[Overseer of Cartel Operations, Tilnes Special Detachment|overseer]], and two other Caarites to be transformed into grotesque, raging [[mutant]]s. Shortly afterward, the Believers initiated an operation to disperse the virus on [[Caarimon]], the Caarite [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], an act that, if successful, would have killed hundreds of thousands of individuals. However, the cultists were prevented from releasing the virus by a group of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance agents]] and the threat of the plague was averted.

==Biology==
===Characteristics===
{{Quote|The Cularin Militia has learned of a plot which, if successful, will result in the deaths of hundreds of thousands of innocents.|Osten Dal'Nay, on the anti-Caarite virus|<ref name="BOB" />}}
The anti-[[Caarite]] virus was a deadly, [[Bioengineering/Legends|bio-engineered]] viral<ref name="CA" /> plague<ref name="Contract AA23">{{LivingForce|Contract AA23 (roleplaying adventure)}}</ref> that was developed to target members of the [[Caarite]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The infection was artificially designed and at a sub-atomic level, the cellular structure of the virus bore a squiggle that served as a signature of the [[Unidentified genetic scientist|genetic scientist]] who had developed the disease. Various different versions of the plague existed and it took the infection's creator a matter of [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] to refine a new version.<ref name="OA" /> The virus was prone to mutation and the [[Cularin Militia]], a paramilitary force active in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]], suspected that these mutations were deliberately controlled by the virus' creator.<ref name="BOB" />

The virus could be [[Death/Legends|killed]] by freezing it, for example through exposure to liquid [[Nitrogen/Legends|nitrogen]]<ref name="OA" /> or an equivalent substance, or alternatively via [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|carbon-freezing]].<ref name="BOB" /> The contagion was difficult to treat and while feasible to develop, without a sample of the original viral agent refining an antivirus required took around a [[Standard week/Legends|week]], even in a properly stocked [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]].<ref name="CA" /> A counteragent to the plague was eventually developed, which neutralized the threat of the use of the contagion as a viral weapon.<ref name="TCWCG" /> Afflicted individuals could also be treated via [[Force healing/Legends|healing]] from a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|user]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="CA" /> an energy field that bound [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] together,<ref name="Core Rulebook">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref> though doing so was only effective for treating non-Caarites affected by the contagion and was achievable only by the healer permanently sacrificing some of their Force strength.<ref name="CA" />

===Transmission===
{{Quote|Its transmission is by air. Touch isn't necessary. It only affects Caarites. It may or may not break down if it's immersed in water, since it looks like it's had a mutagen added to it to shift its vulnerabilities to other chemicals every so often. At least, that was the case with the sample we analyzed.|Osten Dal'Nay, on the anti-Caarite virus|<ref name="BOB" />}}
An early version of the virus tested on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Tilnes]]<ref name="CA" /> in about [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]]<ref name="date" /> could be contracted through respiratory inhalation but was not strictly airborne.<ref name="OA" /> The use of a [[Breath mask/Legends|respirator]] therefore allowed an individual protection from catching this version of the virus.<ref name="CA" /> However, the virus was easily capable of modification to become transmissible through airborne means or via physical contact<ref name="OA" /> and a later version of the virus intended for release on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Caarimon]] was fully airborne and capable of being distributed via release in a planetary [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]].<ref name="BOB" /> Other possible means of spreading the virus were through release in a ventilation system or through the use of explosives to distribute the infection.<ref name="CA" />

A viral agent was developed to facilitate the spread of the infection by allowing it to be transported within gel-packs,<ref name="CA" /> and the virus was [[Color/Legends|green]] in color when carried in a liquid form.<ref name="BOB" /> The infection could also be manifested in a [[Gas/Legends|gaseous]] form and transported in a vial. It was possible through the use of a specific combination of chemicals to change virus to a form where would go dormant when exposed to [[Water/Legends|water]].<ref name="OA" /> However, one sample of the virus that was studied by the [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]] Militia included a mutagen that periodically altered the infection's vulnerabilities to other chemicals. It was therefore unclear whether that particular version of the virus would be neutralized when exposed to water.<ref name="BOB" />

===Symptoms===
{{Quote|It's only deadly to Caarites. I could smear it on my face and it wouldn't do anything, but let a Caarite get one whiff of it and she goes into convulsions and dies fifteen painful minutes later.|Osten Dal'Nay, on the anti-Caarite virus|<ref name="BOB" />}}
The virus was designed to be fatal for Caarites, but could also cause seriously illness in other species.<ref name="CA" /> Caarites infected with the plague would experience severe pain and suffer convulsions before [[Death/Legends|dying]] within fifteen [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] of exposure.<ref name="BOB" /> An early version of the virus released on the moon Tilnes had the<ref name="CA" /> unplanned<ref name="OA" /> effect of causing a small minority of afflicted Caarites become severely [[Mutant|mutated]] instead of being killed. Those Caarites such affected were transformed into raging, cannibalistic beings with a grotesque appearance. These mutated Caarites were increased in height to stand at a 2.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="CA" /> far taller than the average 1 meter size of their species,<ref name="LFCG">''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and elongated heads and widened [[Mouth/Legends|mouths]]. They also gained longer [[Limb/Legends|arms]], improved upper body strength, increased speed, sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] and [[Claw/Legends|claws]] similar to those of a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]],<ref name="CA" /> a species of predatory [[reptomammal]].<ref name="TNEGTAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> These mutations could not be treated or reversed.<ref name="CA" />

Though not fatal to non-Caarites, the virus could make infected individuals of other species severely ill,<ref name="OA" /> though symptoms normally alleviated after breathing clean air for 30 minutes.<ref name="CA" /> Individuals developed immunity to the infection once they had recovered<ref name="OA" /> and some experienced permanent non-harmful mutagenic changes that left them stronger and more durable.<ref name="CA" />

The plague affected non-Caarite species in a variety of ways. [[Human/Legends|Humans]] exposed to the virus would feel nauseous but did not experience significant pain, while [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustans]] and [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshans]] developed a feeling that their skin was unclean and experienced a strong desire to cleanse themselves, but no amount of washing could alleviate the sensation. In [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]], the virus caused individuals to feel as if their [[Hair/Legends|fur]] was itchy, to the point that they were tempted to pull their hair out. Their [[Lung/Legends|lungs]] also felt irritable and they developed a cough.<ref name="CA" />

[[Tarasin]] infected with the virus became yellow in color and developed spots that would pulse in [[Time/Legends|time]] with their [[Heart/Legends|heartbeats]] and which would get brighter when the afflicted individuals were agitated. [[Rodian/Legends|Rodians]] and [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] who contracted the plague felt congested and as if their [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] were cold, while the virus caused [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]] and [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabraks]] to produce a significant amount of saliva, to the point that the amount of liquid in their mouths made it difficult for them to speak. In [[Cerean/Legends|Cereans]], the virus led to individuals alternating between feeling fine and feeling ill, as if a low level fever was affecting one lobe of their [[Brain/Legends|brain]]. The virus also caused Cereans to develop a feeling of thirst.<ref name="CA" />

Other species experienced behavioral changes when afflicted by the virus. [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] developed a strong desire to share secrets, while [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] were caused to feel paranoid and [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorians]] were left feeling spry and full of energy.<ref name="CA" />

==History==
===Testing the virus===
{{Quote|We haven't figured out what it is, but we think it may be viral. We haven't announced it yet&mdash;kinda hoping to get everything settled quiet-like&mdash;but we're under quarantine. Nobody's leaving until the agent is identified.|Nevan Khash, to the heroes of Cularin|<ref name="CA" />}}
During time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Believers]] [[Sith cult]] established themselves as a major force of the criminal underworld of the Cularin [[Star system/Legends|system]]<ref name="CA" /> in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="LFCG" /> The [[Sith cultist/Legends|cultists]] sought to eliminate other competing power groups on Cularin and,<ref name="CA" /> around 21 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="date" /> selected the [[Metatheran Cartel]] trading concern as their first target.<ref name="CA" /> From a secret [[S-Ipsus Believers laboratory|Believer research facility]] in the sub-[[City/Legends|city]] [[S-Ipsus]] on the world [[Genarius]], a [[Gene/Legends|genetic]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] began development of a virus to aid the cultists in their scheme.<ref name="OA" /> The resulting plague was designed to be fatal to Caarites,<ref name="CA" /> a [[Porcine/Legends|porcine]] species<ref name="LFCG" /> who dominated the Metatheran Cartel, and the Believers plotted to use the infection to wipe out the Caarites and curtail the Cartel's influence.<ref name="CA" />

The Believers sought to trial the new virus and selected a [[Metatheran Cartel Tilnes base|Metatheran Cartel base]] deep beneath the surface Tilnes, the moon of Cularin, as an appropriate testing ground. The Cartel's operation on Tilnes was not publicly acknowledged<ref name="CA" /> to avert any bad publicity, because of significant ill-feeling was felt towards the Cartel by the people of Cularin.<ref name="TR">{{LivingForce|Broken Orbits: Tilnes Rising}}</ref> The Believers therefore reasoned that even if the virus was successful in wiping out the inhabitants of the base, the Cartel would not let this information become widely known so as to maintain the veneer of secrecy surrounding their operations on the moon.<ref name="CA" />

The cultists detonated inside the office of [[Ko Bas]], the Cartel base's [[Overseer of Cartel Operations, Tilnes Special Detachment|overseer]], an explosive device containing a chemical agent that carried the virus. From there, the plague entered the facility's ventilation system and spread throughout the base. The explosion triggered an emergency mechanism that sealed the facility's doors, trapping inside the bases's inhabitants, between 100 and 150 Caarite Metatheran Cartel employees. All of the facility's occupants were infected and almost all of them died shortly thereafter, some spending their last moments scratching on the base's door to try to escape. Three of the Cartel employees, Ko Bas, [[U]] and [[G]] survived, transformed by the virus into monstrous mutated beings that bore little semblance to their old selves.<ref name="CA" />

After two weeks had elapsed since the release of the virus, a band of six Believers were assigned to survey the results of the dispersal. In preparation for their mission, the Believer team assembled at a [[Cantina/Legends|bar]] in [[Tolea Biqua]],<ref name="CA" /> a floating city on Genarius.<ref name="LFCG" /> There, they were provided with an explosive device containing gel-packs that held a new batch of the plague. The Believers planned to detonate the bomb the Cartel base in the event that the initial release of the infection had not been successful.<ref name="CA" /> The device was programmed to sent a coded signal to the Believer facility on Genarius in the event that the bomb failed to detonate after a predetermined period of time, which would order the Believes to evacuate the base and destroy all evidence of the virus.<ref name="OA" /> When the cultists arrived at the Cartel facility, an [[Electromagnetic field/Legends|electromagnetic]] pulse emitted from the core of Tilnes caused the entrance to the base to seal again, trapping the Believers inside with the mutant Caarites.<ref name="CA" />

The electromagnetic pulse caused the safety valves that had been containing the virus within the Cartel base to deactivate, allowing the contagion to permeate through the tunnels beneath the surface of Tilnes. Over the next few [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] the viral agent spread into the ventilation system of Tilnes' [[Spaceport/Legends|groundport]]. The contaminant were detected by the [[Verga Mer Mining Company]], a corporation that operated on the moon, and Tilnes was placed under quarantine by the VMMC until the cause and nature of the contagion could be identified.<ref name="CA" />

{{RPG|''[[Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away|Caaried Away]]''}}
The [[heroes of Cularin]], a team of renowned freelance [[Agent/Legends|agents]], were hired by the VMMC [[Supervisor/Legends|supervisor]] [[Nevan Khash]] to investigate the contamination and made their way to the Cartel facility. On entering the base, the operatives contracted the anti-Caarite virus and began to display non-fatal symptoms. The agents recovered the bomb brought by the cultists to the facility to spread the fresh batch of the virus and were attacked by the Believers [[Aris (Human)|Aris]] and [[Osia]], who sought to prevent the agents from sharing knowledge of the virus from the outside world. The freelance operatives survived the attack and subsequently received medical treatment from the Verga Mer Mining Company for their exposure to the virus.<ref name="CA" />
{{Endgame}}

===Confrontation on S-Ipsus===
{{Quote|We learned of this facility from an intercepted transmission. It was designed to produce something to harm or kill us. It was incumbent upon us to remove the threat.|A member of the Metatheran Cartel team sent to destroy the Believers laboratory on S-Ipsus|<ref name="OA" />}}
The heroes of Cularin were asked to keep quiet about their discovery of this viral release on Tilnes.<ref name="OA" /><ref name="Metatheran Caution: Open Aarms">In ''[[Metatheran Caution: Open Aarms|Open Aarms]]'', the identity of the party that requested the [[heroes of Cularin]] to keep quiet about the discovery of the anti-[[Caarite]] virus is not made clear.</ref> However, news of the virus soon became known to the inhabitants of the Cularin system and caused great concern.<ref name="OA" /> The Metatheran Cartel had never been particularly well-liked by the people of Cularin and the reports of a strange new illness with links to the Cartel only heightened the Cartel's unpopularity in the Cularin system.<ref name="2003 Preview">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/swlf20021114lf|text=Living Force 2003 Preview}}</ref> A [[S-Ipsus orbital research facility|research station]] was established above S-Ipsus to study the virus so that it could be countered. At the same time, the Believers continued refining the plague from their own installation on S-Ipsus.<ref name="OA" />

Having produced sufficient quantities of the virus for their campaign against the Caarites, the Believers loaded three [[Starship/Legends|starships]] with the plague at their facility on Genarius, each vessel carrying three [[Metric ton/Legends|tons]] of the virus inside a set of [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tanks]]. The ships then departed for Caarimon, the Caarite [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], where the cultists planned to disperse the plague, traveling there via a circuitous route.<ref name="BOB" /> Around this time, the bomb containing a sample of the virus recovered by the heroes of Cularin on Tilnes was taken to the research station orbiting S-Ipsus that setup to study the pathogen.<ref name="OA" /> Hours after the virus laden ships had departed Genarius,<ref name="BOB" /> the bomb sent out its predetermined coded message to the Believer laboratory, ordering that the base should be evacuated and all evidence pertaining to the anti-Caarite virus destroyed. The cultists then set about closing down their base.<ref name="OA" />

The evacuation message was intercepted by both the Metatheran Cartel and the<ref name="OA" /> [[Oblee]]<ref name="Recursion">{{LivingForce|Belted In: Recursion}}</ref> [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Nirama]]. Concerned that the Believers would destroy a [[Naescorcom/Legends|Narscorcom]] [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] production line beneath which the cultists' research laboratory was situated as cover for their evacuation,<ref name="OA" /> and worried also about the possibility of the [[Factory/Legends|factory's]] [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaught]] workers becoming infected with the illness,<ref name="BOB" /> Nirama dispatched the heroes of Cularin to locate and destroy the laboratory. Meanwhile, the Cartel also sent a team of [[Environment suit/Legends|bio-suit]] clad [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] to raid the Believer facility, hoping to prevent the use of the virus to commit [[Speciecide|genocide]] against the Caarites.<ref name="OA" />

The Cartel strike team entered the base and killed all of the researchers working on the development of the virus. The soldiers then seized all evidence pertaining to the plague that they could lay their hands on, but were unable to locate an active sample of virus. The Believer [[Canduri]], who was among the cultists present at the base, evaded the Cartel forces and fled the laboratory with a vial containing an active sample of the latest strain of the virus.<ref name="OA" />

{{RPG|''[[Metatheran Caution: Open Aarms|Open Aarms]]''}}
The heroes of Cularin apprehended Canduri and her sample of the anti-Caarite virus just as she fled the laboratory. The [[Thaereian military]], an [[Army/Legends|armed force]] that was [[Thaereian Navy charter|enfranchised]] by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to defend the Cularin system, also learned that something was being developed on S-Ipsus that put the entire Cularin system at risk. Shortly after the heroes of Cularin captured Canduri, a [[Thaereian]] [[Navy/Legends|navy]] patrol led by the Bothan [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Mish Paht]] accosted the freelance operatives in S-Ipsus and attempted to seize the sample of the virus recovered from Canduri. The heroes of Cularin evaded the Thaereians and subsequently handed Canduri and the virus specimen over to the Cularin Militia.<ref name="OA" />
{{Endgame}}

Over the next few [[Standard day/Legends|days]], the Militia studied the virus sample and worked with various scientific bodies in the Cularin system to learn more about the plague. Despite the threat posed by the virus, the Cularin Militia did not warn the [[Cularin Government]] or the Metatheran Cartel of the illness, to prevent any Believers within their ranks warning the cult and causing the to accelerate their plans.<ref name="BOB" />

===Attempted release on Caarimon===
{{Quote|Aside from leaving something behind that could kill thousands of us, they seemed very nice.|Patla Soo, on the Believers who transported the anti-Caarite virus to Caarimon|<ref name="BOB" />}}
The three Believer ships that had left Genarius with the plague arrived at Caarimon and the Believers hired the [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[Melo Centris]] to assist them with dispersing the virus on the world. The Believers carried with them equipment supplied by the Thaereian military, and Centris claimed that the Thaereians were providing financial and logistical support to the mission to release the virus, though the Thaereians refuted this allegation. The Cularin Militia learned that the Believers' plan to disperse the virus on Caarimon and [[Osten Dal'Nay]], the leader of the Militia, assigned the heroes of Cularin to prevent the plague being released on the world.<ref name="BOB" />

A group of Believers led by the former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Crymsin Ost]] attacked the Cartel research facility [[Creautaa-V]], a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] Caarimon and released the virus, wiping out all the Caarites on board. From there, the cultists planned to dispatch [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]] containing the virus and detonate them in the planetary atmosphere. To maximise the devastation, the Believers also intended to crash escape pods into a [[Groundquake/Legends|seismically]] sensitive area and trigger a tectonic cataclysm. It was anticipated that the resulting devastation and viral pandemic would cause hundreds of thousands of deaths, wiping out more than half of the Caarite population of Caarimon. In preparation, the cultists hauled several [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] tanks filled with the virus to the lower level of the stations, next to where the escape pods were situated.<ref name="BOB" />

On of the Believer [[Transport/Legends|transports]] that had departed Genarius touched down in the city [[Joventusek]] on Caarimon, docking in the [[Hangar/Legends|landing bay]] [[B-2]] with 100 [[Liter/Legends|liters]] of the virus aboard. Upon the vessel's arrival, the local Cartel forces scanned the presence of a potentially hazardous substance aboard the ship and confiscated the bacta tank containing the virus. Unaware of the true nature of the the substance, the Cartel took the tank to a basement in the office complex [[Cartel Central]] to await analysis.<ref name="BOB" />

{{RPG|''[[Metatheran Caution: Belly of the Beaast|Belly of the Beaast]]''}}
The heroes of Cularin arrived on Caarimon on their quest to thwart the release of the virus and discovered the bacta tank filled with the plague that had been seized by the Cartel. The operatives informed the Cartel forces of the danger posed by the infection and neutralized the virus by carbon freezing it in a facility in Cartel Central. [[Patla Soo]], the manager of Cartel Central was outraged that her superiors in the Cartel had not informed her of the Believers' development of the viral threat and determined to demand an explanation.<ref name="BOB" />

The agents then landed on Creautaa-V just as the Believers were filling escape pods with the virus and prepping them for launch. The operatives subsequently defeated the cultists and prevented the virus from being dispersed. To thank the heroes of Cularin for saving their planet from the virus, a large party was held by the Caarites on Caarimon in honor of the the freelance agents' efforts.<ref name="BOB" />
{{Endgame}}

As a further celebration, the Cartel also organised a party on [[Dorumaa]], a Cularin system moon, to celebrate the preventing of the release of the virus.<ref name="PO">{{LivingForce|Paarty On!}}</ref> A counteragent to the plague was eventually developed from samples of the virus recovered from the contagion's first victims, frustrating the further use of the infection to wipe out the Caarites. With their scheme to counter the Metatheran Cartel in tatters, the Believers abandoned their hideout in the [[Almas Sith fortress|Sith fortress]] of the planet [[Almas]] and went underground.<ref name="TCWCG" />

==Behind the scenes==
The anti-Caarite virus was created by [[Morrie Mullins (real person)|Morrie Mullins]] and featured in all three instalments of the [[Metatheran Caution trilogy]]&mdash;''[[Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away|Caaried Away]]'',<ref name="CA" /> ''[[Metatheran Caution: Open Aarms|Open Aarms]]''<ref name="OA" /> and ''[[Metatheran Caution: Belly of the Beaast|Belly of the Beaast]]''&mdash;<ref name="BOB" />released in [[2003]] as part of [[RPGA]]'s [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|Living Force]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] campaign. The efforts by the heroes of Cularin to thwart the release of the virus served as the main plot arc of the trilogy.<ref name="CA" /><ref name="OA" /><ref name="BOB" /> The virus was first mentioned in the [[Wizards.com]] article "Living Force 2003 Preview", which was published in November [[2002]] and provided details of upcoming arcs of the Living Force campaign.<ref name="2003 Preview" /> It was first identified as the "anti-Caarite virus" in the second instalment of the Metatheran Caution trilogy, ''Open Aarms''.<ref name="OA" />

The virus later received a mention in the [[2009]] roleplaying sourcebook ''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'', which provided new information on the plague<ref name="TCWCG" /> and contradicted ''Belly of the Beaast'' on the means through which the virus was foiled. Whereas in ''Belly of the Beaast'' the virus is prevented from being dispersed on Caarimon by the heroes of Cularin defeating the cultists who sought to release the plague,<ref name="BOB" /> the ''Campaign Guide'' states that the dispersal of their virus was foiled by the development of a counteragent that nullified it.<ref name="TCWCG" /> This article presents both explanations for the means through which the release of the virus was foiled.<ref name="BOB" /><ref name="TCWCG" />

There is a possible mention of the virus in the Wizards.com article ''[[Tilnes Falling]]''. The article served as a tie-in to ''Caaried Away'' and mentions that around the same time as the events of the Metatheran Caution trilogy a couple of workers of the Verga Mer Mining Company contracted a strange mine fever. The article does not provide any further corroboration on whether this is a reference to the anti-Caarite virus,<ref name="TF">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/swlf20030306scenario|text=Tilnes Falling}}</ref> which was released on Tilnes during the events depicted in ''Caaried Away''.<ref name="CA" />

===Roleplaying outcomes===
====''Caaried Away''====
In the Metatheran Caution trilogy, the player characters roleplay as the Heroes of Cularin and the actions and decisions of the players can influence some of the events that occur. In ''Caaried Away'', it is possible for the player characters to contract the virus upon entering the Metatheran Cartel on Tilnes. The adventure lists the symptoms that different species experience when infected with the virus and advises gamemasters&mdash;those directing the flow of the roleplay session&mdash;to be creative if players of species not listed catch the illness, suggesting as an example that [[Ortolan/Legends|Ortolans]] could develop a craving for [[Diet/Legends|diet]] pills.<ref name="CA" />

While the player characters are investigating the Metatheran Cartel base on Tilnes, it is possible for the bomb rigged with the viral agent that was brought to the facility by the Believers to be detonated. In such a scenario, the virus remains present in the containment tubes in what remains of the bomb and a sample can be recovered by the player characters for further study. If the player characters do not recover the bomb or its remains, they can also provide a sample of the virus for further study via the infections existing inside any of the player characters whom contracted the plague. If the Believers Aris and Osia defeat the heroes of Cularin, the two cultists take the bomb containing the viral agent and leave.<ref name="CA" />

Those player characters afflicted by the virus during the events of ''Caaried Away'' can be left with beneficial mutations arising from their exposure to the pathogen that leave them stronger, faster and hardier, providing them improved roleplaying statistics. It is also possible for the player characters to express an interest to the Verga Mer Mining Company in assisting the development of an antivirus to counter the plague, in which case the VMMC grants them a Naescorcom [[P7 trauma kit]] and [[Nilar Med/Tech Corporation]] [[field cauterizer]] to assist their studies into the virus.<ref name="CA" />

====''Open Aarms''====
In ''Open Aarms'' it is possible for the player characters to choose to handover the sample of the anti-Caarite that they capture from the Believer Canduri to various different parties, including the Metatheran Cartel, the Thaereian military, the Cularin Militia or alternatively to the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. The player can also opt to hand the virus over the the research team studying the virus over S-Ipsus, who are very grateful to receive the sample, or to Nirama, who then has the virus sample sent on to someplace more appropriate.<ref name="OA" />

====''Belly of the Beaast''====
During ''Belly of the Beaast'', it is possible for the player characters to fail to learn of or deal with the bacta tank containing the anti-Caarite virus that was confiscated by the Metatheran Cartel in Joventusek. If so, when the heroes of Cularin conform the Believers on the space station Creautaa-V during, it is possible for Melo Centris to use the threat of the virus impounded at Cartel Central as a bargaining chip to facilitate her escape. It is also possible that after the player characters prevent the release of the virus from Creautaa-V, a group of Believers break in Cartel Central and make off with the virus-filled bacta tank stored there. A [[Speeder/Legends|speeder]] chase then ensures across Caarimon as the heroes of Cularin attempted to apprehend the cultists and capture the tank.<ref name="BOB" />

After the player characters prevent the release of the virus from Creautaa-V, the players have the option of neutralizing the escape pods containing the anti-Caarite virus either by dumping the virus into space and firing on it, by carbon freezing it or by turning the virus over to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]],<ref name="BOB" /> the ruling body of the Jedi Order,<ref name="Core Rulebook" /> for them to dispose of. The players can also choose to hand over the virus to another party for further analysis. After the Believers are defeated, it is possible for the people of Caarimon to stage a grand party to celebrate the aversion of the viral threat.<ref name="BOB" />
